title: Weekly Catcher — PM/Eng sync notes (Eli)
content:
Purpose: quick informal notes to prep for the weekly PM↔Eng sync. Keep this as a scratchpad — I will distill into a short agenda message before the meeting.

Top goals for this week's touchpoint:
- Confirm rollout timeline for small-batch dynamic batching on Dedicated (goal: reduce 95th pct latency by 12% without harming p50).
- Decide console UX for model-fallback visibility (how much telemetry we expose to customers vs. internal-only).
- Surface Private deployment checklist gaps discovered in recent on‑prem pilot.
- Triage billing anomaly from last Friday (unexpected token surge for sandbox orgs).

Quick status bullets / things to bring up: 
- Dynamic batcher spike test (serving-runtime): short A/B run complete, promising ~8% 95th reduction but increased p50 by ~3ms. Need to understand regressions at low seq length. Linked PR above.
- Console feature: rollout flag added to config page but UX team wants to hide fallback details behind an "advanced" toggle. I think we should default to minimal info for PLG customers but expose a richer trace in account settings for enterprise.
- Dedicated capacity plan: infra asked for clearer burst policy definition. Current doc (JIRA-4321) doesn't state throttling order across pools — risk of silent failover.
- Private pilot (ACME corp): on‑prem install failed on step 4 (HSM integration). Ops runbook suggests manual key import; need product decision whether to streamline or keep manual for audit trail.
- Billing anomaly: sandbox orgs spiked 3x tokens for two hours. Appears correlated with a misconfigured retry loop in a partner's integration. Need to decide whether to credit customers or clawback.

Questions I want Eli to help unblock (notes for agenda):
1) Dynamic batching decision: do we ship as "opt-in" experimental on Dedicated first, or try default-on with rollout window and automatic rollback? Pros/cons: opt-in lowers blast radius, default gets wins earlier but requires fast rollback.
2) Console telemetry exposure: product tradeoff between transparency and noise. Ask for a short policy: default visibility levels (PLG, Paid, Enterprise) + path to enable detailed fallbacks.
3) Private install UX: trade compliance vs convenience. Ask engineering to estimate dev effort to support an automated HSM handshake flow (ballpark 1 sprint?).
4) Billing remediation: who signs credits? Finance wants a one-off review threshold ($ value) — need PM + Eng agreement on mitigation steps and customer comms.

Proposed agenda (5–10 min per item, 30–40 min total):
- 0–5 min: quick wins & standups (blockers that need immediate help)
- 5–15 min: Dynamic batching experiment review + decision (rollout plan)
- 15–25 min: Console fallback telemetry policy (align on default and enterprise path)
- 25–30 min: Billing anomaly triage (assign owners, decide customer communication)
- 30–40 min: Private pilot HSM issue + next steps (ops + product alignment)
- If time: open items / backlog grooming

Action items I want to capture during/after the meeting: 
- ENG (Samir): produce a short rollback playbook for dynamic-batcher (commands, metrics to watch) — due Wed EOD.
- PM (me): draft console telemetry policy doc and proposed UI copy for "advanced" view — due Thu morning.
- OPS (Maya): reproduce the HSM failure in a sandbox and log exact failure mode + paste runbook diff — due Tue.
- FINANCE (Asha): draft a credit policy proposal for token anomalies (threshold + template comms) — due Fri.

Notes / prompts to keep in mind during discussion: 
- For dynamic batching, sequence length distribution matters a lot. Bring sample histograms for p50/p95 by seq bucket; if p50 shifts are concentrated in short-seq buckets that suggests batching overhead.
- Console visibility: categorize fallback telemetry into three levels: summary (boolean fallback occurred), timeline (per-request trace id + latency), and full-kv (KV cache/params). Decide which levels are default for each customer tier.
- Private: keep auditability first — if we automate HSM key import, preserve explicit customer consent and signed logs.
- Billing: prefer proactive credits for clear platform errors to preserve trust; if partner integration caused it, consider a joint comms plan.

Stuff to collect before meeting (prep checklist):
- Samir: histogram + A/B raw logs + perf dashboard link (attach in Slack)
- Maya: stacktrace from HSM failure and exact package versions used
- Asha: rough estimate of $ exposure for the spike (last Friday window)
- Me: short draft agenda + one‑pager for console telemetry policy

Random scratch ideas (low-priority):
- Consider an "adaptive batcher" that adjusts max batch size at runtime based on tail latency signals rather than fixed heuristics. Might be an R&D spike.
- Explore a small usage-tier toggle in Console that surfaces "experimental features" and auto-enrolls customers who opt-in for early metrics. Could accelerate iteration.

Follow-ups after the meeting (how I'll process notes):
- Convert action items to JIRA tasks and assign owners, link to this scratch doc for context.
- Capture decision log entry in confluence: short rationale, owner, rollback criteria.

Open questions I still have (to add to parking lot):
- If we make fallback traces visible to customers, what liability/PII concerns exist? Who signs off (security/compliance)?
- For Dedicated rollback, what's the expected time to recover under current infra? (SRE input needed)

End-of-note. Will prune and send a tidy agenda message ~1h before the sync.
